sections.heading: Food security — the three pillars and the Indian system

blocks.text: Food security (FAO) = **availability** (production/stocks) + **access** (affordability/entitlement — Amartya Sen's insight that famines are entitlement failures, not food shortages) + **absorption** (nutrition/utilisation — clean water, health). India solved availability (Green Revolution → record ~330+ MT foodgrains) but struggles with access-quality and absorption (stunting ~35%, anaemia ~57% women). The delivery spine: **NFSA 2013** — legal entitlement of **5 kg/person/month** to **75% rural / 50% urban** (~81 crore people; free grains since 2023 as **PMGKAY-integrated**), Antyodaya 35 kg/household; maternal benefits and MDM as statutory rights (Secs 4–5).

rows: Cereal-centric (rice-wheat), regionally skewed; fiscal cost (food subsidy ~₹2 lakh crore)
FCI depots, silo modernisation, OMSS releases

blocks.text: **AP's PDS**: near-universal coverage culture predating NFSA (the state's rice-subsidy tradition since **NTR's ₹2/kg rice, 1983** — the political economy landmark), **doorstep delivery via mobile dispensing units (2021)**, fortified rice rollout, and Anna canteens for cooked-meal access — cite AP as the delivery-innovation case.

sections.heading: Sustainable agriculture — feeding the future without eating it

items: **Why the Green-Revolution model hit limits**: paddy-wheat monoculture, **groundwater over-draft** (subsidised power + MSP assurance), soil fatigue (NPK imbalance ~urea bias), stubble-burning externalities, GHG intensity — productivity plateaued while ecological costs compounded.

**The sustainable toolkit**: micro-irrigation (PMKSY — 'per drop more crop'), **Soil Health Cards & balanced fertilisation (nano-urea, PM-PRANAM incentives)**, crop diversification (millets — **International Year of Millets 2023, 'Shree Anna'**; pulses-oilseeds missions), **natural/organic farming** (NMNF 2023; Paramparagat Krishi), agroforestry, climate-resilient varieties (drought/flood-tolerant), and **ICAR's climate-smart village** approach.

**The AP flagship — APCNF (Community-managed Natural Farming)**: ~8-10 lakh farmers transitioning via SHG-anchored extension (CRPs), zero-budget input logic (bio-stimulants, mulching, pre-monsoon dry sowing), documented input-cost cuts with comparable yields — **the world's largest agro-ecology programme**, cited by UN agencies; balance it with the scientific-scrutiny caveat (yield debates at scale).

**Policy tension to name**: MSP-procurement locks the cereal system that sustainability must unwind — the reform is **remunerating diversification** (price support for pulses/millets, carbon/eco-service payments) rather than exhorting it.

sections.heading: Integrated rural development — from IRDP to Mission Antyodaya

blocks.text: 'Integrated' rural development means attacking **income, infrastructure and human development together** — the lesson from the **IRDP (1978-99)** era's failure (assets without markets, credit without capability → the loan-cow that died). The lineage: IRDP + allied programmes → **SGSY (1999)** (group approach) → **NRLM (2011)** (the AP-SERP SHG architecture nationalised) — plus the platform programmes: **MGNREGA** (wage floor + assets), **PMGSY (1.7+ lakh km of all-weather roads — the single highest-return rural investment by evaluation literature)**, **PMAY-G**, **Jal Jeevan (har ghar jal ~75%+ coverage)**, SAUBHAGYA/DDUGJY (electrification), BharatNet (gram-panchayat fibre) — and the convergence frame of **Mission Antyodaya** (GP-level gap surveys) and **Aspirational Districts/Blocks**.

rows: Roads raise non-farm employment, school continuation, prices realised — the multiplier champion
NRLM SHGs, DDU-GKY skilling, agri-allied value chains
Rural non-farm income share now ~ half — 'rural' no longer equals 'agricultural'
JJM tap water, PMAY-G, SBM-G (ODF+), electrification
Time-poverty and health channels to productivity
Service delivery + market access at village point
Mission Antyodaya, GPDP planning, Aspirational Blocks (500)
Data-ranked, gap-funded local planning — the design frontier

blocks.text: **Regional diversification** (the syllabus phrase) has two Indian senses: (a) **spatially balanced development** — correcting the east-west and intra-state divides (backward-region funds, Aspirational Districts, AP's own north-coastal & Rayalaseema packages); (b) **economic diversification of regions** — moving districts beyond mono-crop/mono-industry dependence (ODOP — One District One Product; agro-processing clusters; rural tourism; GI-tagged crafts like **Etikoppaka toys, Dharmavaram silk, Machilipatnam Kalamkari**).

items: **The stack**: **PMJDN (~53 crore accounts, ~56% women, ~2/3 rural)** → RuPay + ₹2 lakh accident cover → **JAM-DBT** rails → micro-insurance (JJBY/PMSBY) → micro-pension (APY) → credit ladder (**Mudra ~₹27+ lakh crore cumulative**, SHG-bank linkage ~₹7+ lakh crore loans outstanding to ~14 crore families, KCC for farmers/fishers/dairy) → **UPI as the usage engine** (rural adoption via QR ubiquity) → new institutions (Payments Banks — **IPPB's 1.5+ lakh postal touchpoints**, Small Finance Banks) and **Business Correspondents (~30 lakh)** as the human last mile.

**From access to usage to quality**: accounts ~universal (Findex: 78%+ adults), but dormancy, thin credit files, over-indebtedness pockets (microfinance stress belts), and mis-selling risks — the **RBI Financial Inclusion Index (~64 and rising)** tracks access-usage-quality; digital-fraud protection and grievance redress are the new frontier.

**AP's distinctive base**: the **SHG-bank linkage model born in undivided AP (NABARD pilot 1992)**; AP consistently tops SHG credit; secretariat-adjacent **banking correspondents in villages**; Aadhaar-seeded DBT saturation — financial inclusion is AP's strongest inclusion suit.
**Design lesson**: inclusion succeeded where **rails (accounts-Aadhaar-mobile) met reasons (DBT, UPI, SHG credit)** — access alone idles; purpose activates.

sections.heading: AP's inclusive-growth architecture — the saturation-DBT state

blocks.text: AP's model has four pillars: **(1) direct benefit transfers at saturation** (every eligible household, Aadhaar-seeded, calendarised); **(2) doorstep delivery machinery** (village/ward secretariats ~15,000, one per ~2,000 people; volunteers; **Mee-Seva/Spandana** rails); **(3) fee-free human-capital access** (fee reimbursement, education incentives, Aarogyasri health cover, subsidised rice); **(4) women-centred delivery** (transfers to mothers' accounts, SHG federations as the social spine). Scheme names change with governments — **learn functions with both regime labels**: farmer support (**Rythu Bharosa / Annadata Sukhibhava** ~₹20,000/yr incl. PM-KISAN), mothers' education incentive (**Amma Vodi / Talliki Vandanam** ~₹15,000), pensions (**YSR/NTR Bharosa** ~₹4,000/month doorstep), health (**YSR Aarogyasri / NTR Vaidya Seva**, cover expanded toward ₹25 lakh), plus fee reimbursement (Vidya Devena-lineage), housing pattas in women's names, and skill/jobs missions.

sections.heading: Evaluation — the model's power and its bills

items: **Achievements to credit**: MPI/NFHS improvements (poverty incidence among the lower cohort of states), near-zero-leakage transfers (~₹2+ lakh crore DBT cumulative across schemes since 2019), delivery-dignity innovations (doorstep pensions, MDUs), tenancy-inclusive farm support, and the SHG platform's resilience across regimes.

**The bills**: fiscal (revenue deficit financing consumption transfers — the GBA notes' core), **capex crowd-out** (infrastructure gap vs neighbours), scheme discontinuity/renaming costs (beneficiary confusion, MIS churn), volunteer-system's politicisation debate, and the graduation question — transfers stabilise consumption but the **jobs escalator** (industry, services) must come from the growth notes' agenda.

**DWCRA's special place**: Development of Women & Children in Rural Areas (a 1980s IRDP sub-scheme) found its deepest roots in undivided AP — becoming the **cultural institution ('DWCRA groups')** that SERP/Velugu scaled and NRLM nationalised; any AP answer on women/SHGs should trace **DWCRA → Velugu → NRLM** in one line.

**The balanced verdict**: AP proves DBT-saturation **works as welfare technology**; whether it works as **development strategy** depends on pairing it with investment — the state's own Amaravati/ports/corridors bet.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The examiner asks 'AP schemes' but rewards the MODEL — four pillars, DWCRA lineage, saturation logic, and the honest bills. One paragraph of achievements, one of costs, one line of verdict: that's the top-band shape.

prelimsPointers: **DWCRA** (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas, 1982-83) had its strongest roots in undivided AP — ancestor of **Velugu/SERP (2000)** and the NRLM template.
AP's SHG universe: **~9-10 lakh SHGs, ~1 crore women**; interest-free SHG-loan support (Sunna Vaddi lineage).
Village/ward **secretariats (2019)**: ~15,000 units, ~1.3 lakh staff; volunteers at ~50-household ratio.
AP social pensions ~**₹4,000/month with doorstep delivery** — among India's most generous.
Farm support: state top-up integrates **PM-KISAN** to ~₹20,000/yr; **e-crop** enrolment gates input benefits; tenant farmers included via **Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019** cards.
AP PDS: **rice cards near-universal; mobile dispensing units for doorstep ration (2021); fortified rice statewide**.
Health: Aarogyasri-lineage cover expanded (toward ₹25 lakh announcements) + **family doctor programme (2023)**.

From DWCRA to NRLM — trace how undivided AP's women's-group experiment became national policy.
Saturation removes exclusion errors at fiscal cost — assess AP's DBT calendar on coverage, adequacy and sustainability.
PDS in AP is a political institution older than NFSA — analyse its evolution from ₹2/kg rice to doorstep delivery.
Transfers stabilise, jobs transform — what must accompany AP's welfare model for genuine inclusive growth?

glossary.definition: 1980s IRDP sub-scheme organising rural women's income groups — the seed of AP's SHG movement and cultural shorthand for women's collectives in the state.
Calendarised direct transfers to every eligible beneficiary without phased targeting — AP welfare's operating system.
AP's 2019 instrument recognising tenant cultivators for benefits and credit without affecting owner title — tenancy-inclusion by design.
Vehicle-based doorstep delivery of PDS rations — AP's 2021 innovation in distribution dignity.
The challenge of moving households from transfer-supported floors to self-sustaining incomes — welfare's unfinished half.
Describing schemes by what they do rather than their (changing) names — the regime-proof way to study state welfare.
